questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.category: Limits, Continuity & Differentiability :: Advanced Mathematical Structure (Type 1)
questions.question:
Evaluate the indeterminate limit in [Limits, Continuity & Differentiability]:
$$L = \lim_{x \to 0} \left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^{1/x^2}$$
questions.solution: Form is $1^\infty$. $L = \exp\left(\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\frac{\sin x}{x} - 1}{x^2}\right) = \exp\left(\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin x - x}{x^3}\right)$. Taylor expansion gives $\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + O(x^5) \implies \lim \frac{-x^3/6}{x^3} = -\frac{1}{6}$. Hence $L = e^{-1/6}$.
questions.explanation: Solve using rigorous mathematical proofs and transformations in Limits, Continuity & Differentiability.

questions.question:
Evaluate the integer value of the limit in [Limits, Continuity & Differentiability]:
$$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} \times 6$$
questions.solution: Using Taylor series $\sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + O(x^5)$, we have $\frac{x - \sin x}{x^3} = \frac{1}{6} + O(x^2) \to \frac{1}{6}$. Multiplied by $6$, the value is $1$.
questions.explanation: Derive using rigorous mathematical theorems in Limits, Continuity & Differentiability.
